title: The Free Kick (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational soccer philosophy 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal absurdist sport football
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The free kick is a gift the referee has given
A moment twenty-four yards out where something can be driven
The wall lines up and jumps at entirely the wrong moment
The goalkeeper goes left and that was not the best component

[Pre-Chorus]
I've seen free kicks from twenty-five yards clear the crossbar wide
By a margin that suggests the ball had somewhere else to ride

[Chorus]
The free kick knows something I don't know
It knows the angle between the wall and where the keeper'll go
The free kick is a calculation done in under three seconds flat
By a man who trained for twenty years to do exactly that
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The standing over the ball is theatre and everyone knows it
The run-up and the shuffle are designed to misdirect and show it
The arm goes out, the wall is set, the whistle hasn't blown
The free kick is a conversation everyone has on their own

[Bridge]
Sometimes it goes through the gap, sometimes it goes around
Sometimes it deflects off someone and spins into the ground
The free kick has no guarantees and that's the whole appeal
You do the work, you take the kick — the rest is what you feel

[Outro]
Free kick knows… the wall knows too… free kick knows
That's my boy
